Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

campaign noun and verb

an organized effort to win votes or support

also election campaign, canvass, canvassing, run for office, stand for office, bribery (in elections), graft, shake hands (when campaigning), squeeze the flesh, graft (political), bribery (in an election)

classical

Cic. Att. 1.1.1: petītiōnis nostrae
Traupman 178: campaign, petītiō
Traupman 286

petītiō, petītiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a candidacy, an election campaign

Other words

  • ambiō, ambīre, ambīvī, ambītum — canvass, go round for votes

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 178, 286: campaign, ambiō; Traupman 286

  • prēnsō, prēnsāre, prēnsāvī, prēnsātum — canvass, go round shaking hands

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.1: prēnsat ūnus P. Galba; Traupman 180: manūs prēnsāre, shake hands when campaigning

  • ambitiō, ambitiōnis f. — canvassing (by lawful means)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.62: quid dē nostrīs ambitiōnibus loquar? (Lewis & Short)

    Lawful canvassing; ambitus is the unlawful kind.

  • ambitus, ambitūs m. — electoral bribery, unlawful canvassing

    noun, fourth declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 178: illegal campaign practices, ambitus; Traupman 179: graft; Traupman 323

    Not a campaign but the crime, as in lēx dē ambitū.

Examples

  • petītiōnis nostrae, quam tibi summae cūrae esse sciō, hujus modī ratiō est, quod adhūc conjectūrā prōvidērī possit. prēnsat ūnus P. Galba

    as for my campaign, which I know matters a great deal to you, this is how it stands, as far as one can guess so far: only Publius Galba is canvassingCic. Att. 1.1.1

See also election, vote, office, political, campaign.
